The '''Papkovich&ndash;Neuber solution''' is a technique for generating analytic solutions to the [[Newtonian fluid|Newtonian]] incompressible [[Stokes flow|Stokes equations]], though it was originally developed to solve the equations of [[linear elasticity]]. It was derived independently in the early 1930s and named after {{Interlanguage link|Peter Feodorovich Papkovich|de|Pjotr Fjodorowitsch Papkowitsch}}<ref>{{Citation |last=Papkovish |first=P. F. |title=Solution Générale des équations differentielles fondamentales d'élasticité exprimée par trois fonctions harmoniques |periodical=Compt. Rend. Acad. Sci. Paris |volume=195 |pages=513&ndash;515 |year=1932}}.</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Papkovich |first=P. F. |title=The representation of the general integral of the fundamental equations of elasticity theory in terms of harmonic functions |periodical=Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR, Phys.-Math. Ser. |volume=10 |issue=1425 |pages=90 |year=1932}}</ref> and {{Interlanguage link|Heinz Neuber|de}}.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Neuber |first=H. |date=1934 |title=Ein neuer Ansatz zur Lösung räumlicher Probleme der Elastizitätstheorie. Der Hohlkegel unter Einzellast als Beispiel |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/zamm.19340140404 |journal=ZAMM - Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics / Zeitschrift für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik |language=en |volume=14 |issue=4 |pages=203–212 |doi=10.1002/zamm.19340140404 |issn=0044-2267|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

It can be shown that any [[Stokes flow]] with body force <math>\mathbf{f}=0</math> can be written in the form:

:<math>\mathbf{u} = {1\over{2 \mu}} \left[ \nabla ( \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{\Phi} + \chi) - 2 \mathbf{\Phi} \right]</math>
:<math>p = \nabla \cdot \mathbf{\Phi}</math>

where <math>\mathbf{\Phi}</math> is a [[Harmonic function|harmonic]] vector potential and <math>\chi</math> is a harmonic scalar potential.  The properties and ease of construction of harmonic functions makes the Papkovich–Neuber solution a powerful technique for solving the Stokes Equations in a variety of domains.
